Headline: KSBBL Partners with Kantipur Dental College for Healthcare Discounts
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited has signed an agreement with Kantipur Dental College, Teaching Hospital, and Research Center to provide healthcare fee discounts. Under this agreement, the bank’s employees and customers can receive up to 15% off on various hospital services.
Customers can easily avail themselves of this benefit by presenting proof of their association with the bank. The bank believes this initiative will offer special advantages to all its affiliated clients. The agreement was signed by KSBBL Kathmandu Regional Head Kedar Nath Sharma and the hospital’s Director, Dr. Pratiksha Shrestha.

Headline: KSBBL Provides Scholarships to Needy Students of Durbar High School
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL), under its corporate social responsibility program, provided scholarships to economically disadvantaged students of Durbar High School (Bhanu Secondary School), Ranipokhari, on the occasion of the school’s 172nd foundation and Parents’ Day.
The initiative aims to support deserving students whose studies are affected by financial constraints, with the bank reaffirming its commitment to continue contributing to the education sector through similar social programs in the future.

Headline: KSBBL Successfully Allots 9% Irredeemable Preference Shares
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL) has completed the allotment of its 9% Irredeemable Non-Cumulative Preference Shares on Magh 21, 2082 at NIMB Ace Capital, Lazimpat. The Rs. 35 crores issue received over 1.9 times subscription, reflecting strong investor confidence.
Issued to institutional investors through a private placement, this marks the first-ever irredeemable non-cumulative preference share issued by a development bank in Nepal. The bank expressed gratitude to regulators, applicants, and all stakeholders for their support.

Headline: Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Reports 22.34% Growth in Net Profit and Elevated Earnings Per Share for Q2
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL)
has unveiled its unaudited financial results for the second quarter of FY 2082/83, showcasing a 22.34% rise in net profit, totaling Rs 39.45 crores incomparison to the equivalent period in the previous fiscal year, during which the bank had recorded a net profit of Rs. 32.24 Crores.
Net interest income grew by 11.19%, while impairment charges declined by 4.74%.The bank’s total paid-up capital stands at Rs 3.86 Arba, with reserves of Rs 1.94 Arba and retained earnings of Rs 29.57 crores. Distributal Profit has aslo declined by 21.25%, reaching Rs 29.57 crores , while loans and advances increased by 4.06%, totaling Rs 52.1 Arba.
Key metrics for the quarter include an annualized Earnings Per Share (EPS) of Rs 20.43, a price-earnings (P/E) ratio of 22.17 times, and a net worth per share of Rs 158.07. As of the second quarter, the bank’s capital adequacy ratio stood at 12.57 percent.

Headline: Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Organizes Free Health Camp at Devghat on Maghe Sankranti
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL) organized a free health camp at the religious pilgrimage site of Devghat on the auspicious occasion of Maghe Sankranti. The camp provided breast cancer awareness, blood pressure checks, and diabetes testing with technical support from Bharatpur Hospital and B.P. Koirala Memorial Cancer Hospital.
More than 300 people benefited from the health screenings, consultations, and medical advice. The initiative aimed to promote early detection of health issues, raise health awareness, and support disease prevention within the community. Residents welcomed the program and expressed appreciation to the bank and healthcare professionals for their contribution.

Headline: Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Supports School in Surkhet with Chairs and Warm Clothes
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL), under its Corporate Social Responsibility initiative, distributed chairs and warm clothes to Shree Kopila Secondary School in Birendranagar Municipality–09, Parseni, Surkhet through its Surkhet branch. Branch Manager Sunil Acharya handed over 80 chairs to the school and warm clothing to 80 students.
The support is expected to benefit underprivileged and poor students, especially during the winter season, by enhancing comfort, safety, and confidence. School Principal Tek Narayan Upadhyay expressed gratitude to the bank for its humanitarian support. The bank has reaffirmed its commitment to continue such social initiatives in coordination with stakeholders in the future.

Headline: Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Supports Community Health Center with Water Dispenser in Jhapa
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL), under its Corporate Social Responsibility initiative, has donated a water dispenser to the Basic Health Center located in Mechinagar Municipality–08, Srijana Chowk, Jhapa, through its Ittabhatta branch. The handover was conducted by Koshi Province Head Khim Lal Bhusal in the presence of Ward Chairperson Giriraj Dhamala.
Health Center Chief Diwakar Paudel expressed confidence that the support would benefit all patients, especially the poor and underprivileged, and thanked the bank for its contribution. The bank has reaffirmed its commitment to continue such social initiatives in coordination with stakeholders in the future.

Headline: Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Distributes Warm Supplies to Vulnerable in Lamki
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL), through its Lamki branch, distributed warm blankets, mattresses, bedding, and other winter essentials to the elderly and orphaned children at Lamki Manavsewa Ashram, Kailali, as part of its corporate social responsibility initiative.
Branch head Bhim Raj Jaisi handed over the materials to the Ashram’s director Binod Thapa, who expressed gratitude and highlighted the positive impact on the recipients’ warmth, safety, and morale. The event was attended by bank staff, Ashram officials, and local community members. KSBBL plans to continue such social initiatives in coordination with stakeholders in the future.

Headline: Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Announces Research Grants for MPhil and Master’s Scholars
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited has announced a research grant program for students pursuing MPhil and Master’s degrees in Management, Economics, Business, and IT-related fields at Nepali universities. The initiative aims to promote quality research focused on banking, economic development, digital transformation, innovation, and financial practices in emerging markets.
Eligible scholars can receive financial support for research-related expenses, with grants of up to NPR 100,000 for MPhil students (two scholars) and up to NPR 50,000 per Master’s proposal (up to four scholars). Applicants must submit a 5–7 page concept note to the bank by 14 March 2026. Proposals will be evaluated based on relevance, originality, feasibility, and potential impact on policy and banking practices.

Headline: KSBBL Distributes Warm Clothes to Chepang Children in Rapti Municipality
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL) distributed warm clothes to 70 underprivileged children of the Chepang community studying in grades 1–3 at Shree Bhavishya Nirman Primary School, Rapti Municipality-12, through its Khurkhure branch. Narayangadh Regional Head Surendra Bhandari highlighted the initiative’s positive impact on children’s health and education.
Local leaders, school management, parents, and bank staff attended the program, appreciating KSBBL’s ongoing social responsibility efforts. The bank reaffirmed its commitment to continue such community-focused initiatives in the future.

Headline: KSBBL Successfully Conducts Community Social Responsibility Programs
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL) successfully carried out social responsibility programs in the Butwal area.
Through its Bhairahawa branch, the bank donated three beds to Lumbini Visually Impaired Orphanage, and via its Manigram branch, it provided warm clothes to Shanti Namuna Secondary School for underprivileged students.
Bank officials and local representatives participated in the events, with recipient organizations expressing gratitude. KSBBL plans to continue such community-focused initiatives in the future.

Headline: Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Supports Children’s Welfare with Food and Educational Supplies
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL) donated food and educational materials to the Breathe of Life Children’s Home through its Biratchowk branch as part of its corporate social responsibility.
The supplies were handed over by KSBBL Koshi Province Head Mr. Khimalal Bhusal to the home’s director, Ms. Nirmala Rai.
The initiative aims to support underprivileged children’s basic needs, education, and future prospects. Local officials, bank staff, and stakeholders attended the event. The bank plans to continue such programs in coordination with the community.

Headline: Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Supports Community School with Educational Materials in Kaski
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL), under its Corporate Social Responsibility program, distributed educational and stationery materials to Shree Laxmi Basic School located in Annapurna-3, Paundur, Kaski. The materials were handed over by the bank’s Pokhara Regional Head, Mr. Shiva Kumar Dhakal, to the school’s Principal, Mr. Tara Nath Paudel.
The principal expressed that the support would have a positive impact on improving educational access for students from economically disadvantaged backgrounds and would motivate them in their studies. The program was attended by bank staff, school teachers, students, parents, and other stakeholders. The bank also reaffirmed its commitment to continue similar community-focused initiatives in the future.

Headline: Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Distributes Fiber Blankets to Underprivileged Families in Lahan
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Ltd. has distributed fiber sheets to poor, Dalit, and marginalized families in Ward No. 5 of Lahan Municipality during the winter season to the families of Lahan Municipality Ward No. 5 as part of its Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiative.
The distribution was led by the bank’s Madhesh Province Head, Shyam Chawain to poor and vulnerable households in coordination with the local ward office. Local representatives and bank officials were present during the distribution program.
The bank stated that it remains committed to supporting communities through similar social responsibility programs in the future.

Headline: Kamana Sewa Bank Supports Underprivileged Students with Uniforms and Study Materials
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Ltd. distributed school uniforms and educational materials to underprivileged students of Shree Ramkosh Phoolbari Secondary School in Syangja under its corporate social responsibility initiative.
The support was handed over through the bank’s Birauta branch, with bank officials and school representatives expressing that the assistance would significantly help students and contribute to social development. The bank also committed to continuing similar educational support programs in the future.

Headline: Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Provides Water Purifiers and Dispensers to Health Centers
Full Content:
Under its Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiative, Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited has provided water purifiers and dispensers to two health centers in Jhapa. The bank handed over one unit each to the Basic Health Center in Damak Municipality–5 and the Community Health Center in Kamal Rural Municipality–5, Simple.
The equipment was formally handed over by the bank’s Koshi Province Head, Khim Lal Bhusal, to the respective ward chairpersons. Local representatives expressed confidence that the support will benefit all service recipients visiting the health centers and thanked the bank for its social contribution. Bank officials and local representatives were present during the handover program.

Headline: Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Provides Computer Support to Nepal Bar Association
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank
has provided computer equipment to the Nepal Bar Association, Ramshah Path, to support the continuation of its office operations. The assistance was extended after the Association’s building and premises suffered damage during vandalism and arson incidents that occurred amid a youth-led movement on Bhadra 23 and 24, 2082.
The computers were handed over by the Bank’s Head of Legal Department and Advocate, Dandapani Bhattarai, to the President of the Nepal Bar Association, Senior Advocate Prof. Dr. Vijay Prasad Mishra. Expressing appreciation, Prof. Dr. Mishra stated that the support would play an important role in resuming and facilitating the Association’s work.
Speaking on the occasion, Advocate Bhattarai said the Bank was pleased to collaborate with the Nepal Bar Association in contributing to the development of a progressive society. The handover ceremony was attended by the Bank’s Head of CSR Department, Sushil Poudel, General Secretary of the Nepal Bar Association, Senior Advocate Kedar Prasad Koirala, along with other officials and representatives.

Headline: 10% Bonus Shares of Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Listed in NEPSE
Full Content:
35,10,846.20 unit bonus shares of
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL)
have been listed in NEPSE.
The company convened it's 19th AGM on 24th Ashwin, 2082, and endorsed a 15.7895% dividend for FY 2081/82. The company decided to distribute a 10% bonus share and a 5.7895% cash dividend (including tax). The same bonus shares are now listed in NEPSE.

Headline: KSBBL Partners with Caffeophilia to Offer 10% Discount to Customers and Staff
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL) has signed an agreement with Caffeophilia located in Gyaneshwor, Kathmandu, to offer service charge discounts.
Under this partnership, the bank’s employees and customers can enjoy a 10% discount on food and beverages by presenting proof of their affiliation with the bank.
KSBBL believes this collaboration will provide special benefits to its valued customers. The agreement was signed by the bank’s Marketing Head, Parma Dhungel, and Caffeophilia’s franchise owner, Sadiksha Shrestha.

Headline: KSBBL Partners with Paras Hospital to Offer Up to 50% Discount for Customers and Employees
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL) has signed an agreement with Paras Hospital in Biratnagar, Morang, to offer up to 50% discount on hospital services for the bank’s employees and customers.
Eligible customers can avail the discount by providing proof of their association with the bank. The agreement was signed by KSBBL’s Koshi Province Chief Khimlal Bhusal and Paras Hospital Chairman Safiur Rahman.

Headline: SEBON Approves Issuance of Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank’s Preference Shares
Full Content:
The Securities Board of Nepal (SEBON) has granted approval to Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank for the issuance of 35 lakh non-redeemable cumulative preference shares with a par value of Rs. 100 and a 9% dividend rate. The proposal, endorsed by the bank’s 18th Annual General Meeting and later cleared by Nepal Rastra Bank, has now received the regulatory green light from SEBON.
According to the bank, the issuance will strengthen its capital base and support broader business expansion by enhancing its capital adequacy position. With current market liquidity conditions and prevailing returns, the bank believes that the 9% dividend rate makes this preference share an appealing option for institutional investors.
Nepal Rastra Bank had recently allowed banks and financial institutions to issue non-redeemable cumulative preference shares as an alternative to rights shares for capital augmentation. SEBON’s approval of Kamana Sewa’s issuance marks a meaningful step in translating this policy into practice.

Headline: KSBBL Receives SAFA Certificate of Merit Award 2024
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL) has been honored with the “Certificate of Merit Award” under the financial services category by the South Asian Federation of Accountants (SAFA) for 2024. The award was granted based on the bank’s annual report for FY 2023/24, recognizing its financial transparency, accountability, and governance.
The award was presented during a ceremony in Islamabad, Pakistan. KSBBL had also won an SAFA award last year. SAFA, a network partner of the International Federation of Accountants, includes accounting bodies from Nepal, India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, the Maldives, and Afghanistan. Additionally, the bank’s report had earlier won the “Gold Award” in the financial services category at the National Best Presented Report Award 2024 by ICAN Nepal.

Headline: Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Partners with Hotel Sabrina to Offer Exclusive 10% Customer Discount
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL) has signed an agreement with Hotel Sabrina in Budhanilkantha to provide a 10% service fee discount to its customers and employees. The offer applies to accommodation and food & beverage services, aiming to enhance lifestyle benefits beyond traditional banking.
Customers can easily access the discount by presenting KSBBL cards, the KS iMobile app, or an employee ID. The partnership strengthens customer loyalty, promotes digital banking use, and supports local business collaboration. The agreement was officially signed by KSBBL’s Head of Marketing, Prema Dhungel, and Hotel Sabrina’s Operations Manager, Samir Thapa.

Headline: Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Marks 19th Anniversary with Blood Drive, Futsal Cup, and New ‘AlphaGrow’ Scheme
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL) has celebrated its 19th anniversary by organizing various programs nationwide. On Kartik 27, the bank conducted a large-scale blood donation campaign across its central and regional offices, collecting 429 pints of blood. The events were inaugurated by board member Bhim Prasad Tulachan in Butwal and Deputy CEO Binay Dahal in Kathmandu.
The bank also hosted the 5th Inter-Bank and Financial Institutions Futsal Cup, where Siddhartha Bank (men's category) and Lumbini Bikas Bank (women's category) emerged winners. Additionally, branches in Amar Singh and Pokhara New Road conducted financial literacy programs.
Marking the anniversary, KSBBL launched a new deposit product “AlphaGrow”, targeted at children up to 18 years. The account offers attractive piggy banks and life insurance coverage up to Rs. 50,000, with premiums paid by the bank until the account holder turns 18, promoting savings habits and future financial security for children.

Headline: Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Concludes 5th Futsal Cup on Its 19th Anniversary
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL) celebrated its 19th anniversary by concluding the 5th season of the Kamana Sewa Futsal Cup on Saturday. In the men’s final, Siddhartha Bank defeated Prime Commercial Bank 2-0 to claim the title, while in the women’s final, defending champion Lumbini Bikas Bank beat Global IME Bank 1-0 to win the championship.
A total of 17 men’s teams and 9 women’s teams participated in the tournament. Winners and runners-up were awarded trophies, medals, and certificates. The event was inaugurated by DCEO Binay Dahal, with prizes distributed by COO Bikash Dhungana, and attended by various bank officials and staff. As part of its anniversary celebrations, KSBBL will also organize a nationwide blood donation program on November 27.

Headline: Kamana Sewa Launches Nepal’s First Doorstep Banking Service to Boost Financial Inclusion
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL) has introduced Nepal’s first-ever Doorstep Banking Service (DSBS), approved by the Nepal Rastra Bank, aiming to make banking more accessible, convenient, and inclusive. Launched on October 15, 2025, the service allows customers to conduct cash transactions, account servicing, and document handling directly at their home or office. By leveraging digital tools like the bank’s mobile app, DSBS combines technology with personalized service to simplify banking, especially for busy professionals, senior citizens, differently-abled individuals, and other underserved groups.
Focusing on financial inclusion, the service addresses geographic and mobility barriers, particularly in rural or isolated areas, and promotes digital literacy by offering an assisted-digital banking experience. Initially available in the Kathmandu Valley, KSBBL plans nationwide expansion, positioning DSBS as a transformative step in making formal financial services accessible to all segments of Nepali society.

Headline: Sudeep Acharya Takes Oath as Chairman of Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank
Full Content:
Sudeep Acharya, elected as chairman of Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited during the bank’s 19th Annual General Meeting (AGM), formally took the oath of office and secrecy on Tuesday before Deputy Governor Bam Bahadur Mishra of Nepal Rastra Bank.
The AGM also saw the unopposed election of founder group members Sudeep Acharya, Bhim Prasad Tulachan, Chaturakhar Adhikari, and general group members Balaram Baral, Bishweshwar Subedi, and Dr. Pawan Kumar Sharma to the board for the next four years.
The oath-taking ceremony was attended by senior officials from Nepal Rastra Bank, including Executive Directors Guru Prasad Paudel and Satyendra Timilsina, along with directors and chief executives from development banks.

Headline: Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Holds 19th AGM, Approves 15.7895% Dividend and Elects Board Members
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL) conducted its 19th Annual General Meeting on Ashwin 24, 2082, at Lisara Reception, Naxal, Kathmandu, chaired by Chairman Sudip Acharya. The AGM approved a total dividend of 15.7895%, comprising 10% bonus shares and 5.7895% cash dividend (including tax). The meeting also ratified the annual financial statements for FY 2081/82, including balance sheet, profit and loss account, cash flow, and related schedules.
For the next four years, founder group members Sudeep Acharya, Bhim Prasad Tulachan, Chaturakhar Adhikari, and general group members Balaram Baral, Bishweshwar Subedi, Dr. Pawan Kumar Sharma were elected unopposed to the board. The AGM appointed NBSM and Associates as auditors for FY 2082/83. Shareholders’ queries were addressed by Chairman Sudip Acharya and CEO Dinesh Thakali, who emphasized the bank’s commitment to sustainable returns and continued dividend distribution.

Headline: Sudeep Acharya Re-elected Chairman of Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank
Full Content:
Sudip Acharya has been re-elected as Chairman of Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited by the bank’s 401st Board Meeting, held after the 19th Annual General Meeting. He had previously served as the bank’s chairman.
During the AGM, for the next four years, founder group members Sudeep Acharya, Bhim Prasad Tulachan, Chaturakhar Adhikari, and general group members Balaram Baral, Bishweshwar Subedi, Dr. Pawan Kumar Sharma were elected unopposed to the board.

Full Content:

The initiative aims to improve patient comfort, providing access to clean drinking water and convenient mobile charging during hospital visits.
The donation was formally handed over by KSBBL’s Koshi Province Head to the hospital’s Senior Administrative Officer, highlighting a collaborative commitment to community welfare. This effort is part of KSBBL’s broader CSR vision, which supports health, education, and social welfare projects across Nepal. By addressing immediate needs and enhancing healthcare services, the bank sets a model for other financial institutions to make tangible, positive impacts on local communities.

Headline: KSBBL and Namaste Public Hospital Partner to Offer 20% Healthcare Discount
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL) has signed an agreement with Namaste Public Hospital in Damak, Jhapa, to provide up to 20% discount on hospital services for the bank’s employees and customers. This initiative aims to make healthcare more accessible to the general public.
Eligible individuals can easily avail the discount by presenting proof of their association with the bank. The agreement was signed by KSBBL Province Chief Khimalal Bhusal and Namaste Public Hospital Chairman Kuber Bhattarai, ensuring special benefits for all associated with the bank.

Headline: Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Becomes the First Development Bank to Declare Dividend
Full Content:
"Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL)"
has announced a total dividend of 15.7895% from its accumulated profits for the fiscal year 2081/82. This includes 10% bonus shares and 5.7895% cash dividend (inclusive of tax) which will be received by their respective shareholders.
The declaration follows approval from the bank’s Board of Directors, as confirmed by CEO Dinesh Thakali at a meeting held at the central office on Sunday at 4 PM.
This is a notable move, as the bank become first development bank to announce dividend for FY 2081/82. In the previous fiscal year, the bank had declared a 12% total dividend. The dividend will be paid out to shareholders upon receiving approval from Nepal Rastra Bank and endorsement at the upcoming 19th Annual General Meeting.

Headline: Comprehensive Analysis of Fourth Quarter Reports for FY 2081/82: A Closer Look at Development Banks in Nepal
Full Content:
The fourth-quarter reports for the fiscal year 2081/82 have been publicly disclosed by 15 out of 16 development banks. These reports provide a comprehensive overview of their financial health. Karnali Development Bank Limited has not published its report as Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB) has declared it a "problematic institution" and placed its management under direct NRB control. Share trading of Karnali Development Bank has also been suspended.
This analysis aims to meticulously evaluate the financial performance of Nepal's development banks, categorized as "B" class financial institutions, using the unaudited third-quarter reports for the 2081/82 fiscal year.
The Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE) currently lists 16 development banks, divided into National-level and Regional-level entities. Our focus is on assessing the performance of these "B" class financial institutions, drawing insights from the recently released quarter-end reports.
Net profit:
As per the quarterly report, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has reported the highest net profit for the period, amounting to Rs. 153.74 Crores. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) comes in second place in terms of profit, which amounts to Rs. 131.04 Crores.
The third position is secured by Shine Resunga Development Bank (SHINE) with a net profit of Rs.68.86 Crores. In terms of growth in net profit, Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) achieved the highest growth margin of 201.97% for Q4 of FY 81/82.
At the regional level, Sindhu Bikas Bank (SINDU) reported the highest growth in net profit at 287.60% for Q4 of FY 81/82.
Paid-up capital:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has the highest paid-up capital amounting to Rs. 7.04 Arba among all the development banks, with Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) holding the second-highest paid-up capital at Rs. 5.68 Arba.
On the other hand, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has the lowest paid-up capital of Rs. 26.25 Crores.
Reserve and surplus:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) reported the highest reserve and surplus, totaling Rs. 4.92 Arba. Following MNBBL is Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL) with a reserve of Rs. 3.03 Arba. Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) holds the third position with a reserve of 2.9 Arba.

Headline: KSBBL Partners with Lemon Tree Premier to Offer Exclusive Discounts to Customers and Staff
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL) has signed an agreement with Lemon Tree Premier, Budhanilkantha, Kathmandu, to offer special discounts to its employees and customers.
Under the agreement, customers can enjoy 15% off on accommodation, food, and beverages, and 20% off at the spa by presenting proof of their association with the bank.
The deal was signed by Kedar Nath Sharma, KSBBL Kathmandu Regional Head, and Yadav Prasad Pandey, Chief Operating Officer of the hotel.

Headline: KSBBL Donates Printer to Butwal Police Office, Strengthening Community Support Initiatives
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL) donated a printer to the Butwal District Police Office as part of its corporate social responsibility program. The handover was led by KSBBL director Bhim Prasad Tulachan to DSP Indra Bahadur Rana, in a ceremony attended by police inspectors, bank staff, and regional head Hemanta Babu Acharya.
DSP Rana highlighted that the printer will support services for women, children, and senior citizens, enhancing office efficiency. Director Tulachan emphasized the bank’s commitment to community development and continued collaboration with Nepal Police for societal progress.

Headline: Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Partners with Mahendra Narayan Nidhi Memorial Hospital to Offer Service Discounts
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank has signed an agreement with Mahendra Narayan Nidhi Memorial Hospital in Kathmandu, Basundhara, to provide up to 15% discount on hospital services for the bank’s employees and customers.
The discount can be easily availed by presenting proof of affiliation with the bank. The bank expects all its stakeholders to benefit from this special arrangement. The agreement was signed by Kedar Nath Sharma, Kathmandu Regional Head of the bank, and Kapil Gyawali, Chairman of the hospital.

Headline: Kamana Sewa Bank Partners with Skywalk Nepal to Offer 25% Adventure Discount
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited has partnered with Skywalk Nepal to offer a 25% discount on tickets for both its customers and employees. This initiative, launched through a formal MoU signed in Kathmandu, aims to promote domestic adventure tourism while enhancing customer engagement and employee benefits.
Skywalk Nepal, located in Kamaladi, is a unique glass walkway attraction offering 360-degree views of Kathmandu Valley. The discount can be availed by presenting proof of affiliation with the bank. Both parties expressed optimism about further collaborations, such as promotional events and seasonal campaigns. The partnership reflects the bank’s evolving focus on lifestyle integration, aiming to provide value beyond banking while contributing to the revival of local tourism.

Headline: Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Wins Gold at National Annual Report Awards 2024
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL) has received the Gold Award in the financial services category at the National Best Presented Annual Report Award 2024, organized by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nepal (ICAN).
The award recognizes the bank’s excellence in financial transparency, accountability, and governance for its FY 2023/24 report. Presented during an event in Kathmandu, the report is also nominated for the SAFA BPA Awards. Last year, the bank received the Silver Award from ICAN and a Certificate of Merit from SAFA.

Headline: Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Posts 9.19% Net Profit Growth, EPS at Rs 18.10; Core Revenue Up by 5.25%
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL)
has unveiled its unaudited financial results for the quarter end of FY 2081/82, showcasing a 9.19% rise in net profit, totaling Rs 63.52 crores.
This marks a significant improvement from Rs 58.18 crores in the same period of the previous year. Net interest income grew by 5.25%, while impairment charges inclined by 16.55%.
The bank’s total paid-up capital stands at Rs 3.51 Arba, with reserves of Rs 1.78 Arba and retained earnings of Rs 60.74 crores. Deposits rose by 6.38%, reaching Rs 62.83 Arba, while loans and advances increased by 8.67%, totaling Rs 49.96 Arba.
Key metrics for the quarter include an annualized Earnings Per Share (EPS) of Rs 18.10, a price-earnings (P/E) ratio of 27.69 times, and a net worth per share of Rs 168.13. Additionally, the bank reported a distributable profit of Rs 60.74 crores.

Headline: Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Supports Pashupati Area with 5,000 Shoe Bags and 1,000 Tokens
Full Content:
As part of its corporate social responsibility (CSR) program, Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank has donated 5,000 shoe bags and 1,000 tokens to the Pashupati Area Development Trust. The donation aims to help manage devotees’ footwear in an organized and secure manner, especially during the upcoming Shrawan month, when visitor numbers surge at the Pashupatinath Temple.
The items were handed over by the bank's Credit Administration Head, Parma Dhungel, to Acting Member Secretary Subash Chandra Joshi of the Trust. Joshi expressed gratitude, noting that the donation would greatly aid in managing the footwear of large crowds during peak pilgrimage periods.
Speaking at the event, Dhungel highlighted the bank’s commitment to community welfare and mentioned that Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank, operating through 130 branches nationwide, regularly undertakes various CSR initiatives to support social and cultural institutions.

Headline: Kamana Sewa Introduces Instant Fixed Deposit Loan via Mobile App for Seamless Banking
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited has introduced a digital loan facility for fixed deposit account holders through its mobile banking app ‘KS iMobile’. Customers can now apply for and receive loans against their fixed deposits instantly, without visiting a branch or submitting paperwork.
This move aims to simplify banking, save time, and enhance customer convenience. The bank continues to advance its digital services, including online account opening, video KYC, and mobile banking, supporting its vision of reducing branch dependency and promoting financial inclusion across Nepal.

Headline: Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Provides Financial Literacy to the Visually Impaired in Kathmandu
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited, in collaboration with the Sarwodaya Project and Inclusive Letters and Research, conducted a financial literacy program for visually impaired individuals in Kathmandu. The session, led by the bank’s Head of Branding and CSR, Sushil Poudel, focused on essential topics such as savings, budgeting, financial discipline, investment planning, digital transactions, and online fraud awareness.
Over 40 visually impaired participants attended the event. Sharing personal experiences, Krishna Khatri Abiral stated that due to a lack of timely financial knowledge, he previously avoided banking and relied on others to manage his savings, which led to uncertainty. However, after the session, participants expressed increased confidence in using banking services independently.
Bikram Patharia, another visually impaired attendee, noted that the program instilled hope in the power of small savings to lead to significant financial growth.
Sarwodaya Project representative Saugat Wagle, himself visually impaired, praised the bank for providing inclusive services such as mobile banking and ATM cards to visually impaired customers, helping them enjoy secure financial access like others.
In a move toward inclusive banking, Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank announced the introduction of the "Swabhimaan Savings Account" tailored for visually impaired individuals. This account offers services like ATM and mobile banking without requiring extra documentation or a witness. Importantly, account terms will also be available in Braille, ensuring accessible and independent financial management for visually impaired customers.

Headline: Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Supports Students in Mechinagar Through CSR Initiative
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited recently organized a corporate social responsibility (CSR) program at Shree Saraswati Primary School in Mechinagar, Jhapa, providing educational materials and school bags to 40 students from Nursery to Grade 5. The donation, which included notebooks, pencils, pens, and other essential supplies, aimed to support students from underprivileged backgrounds.
The event was coordinated with the school and attended by Branch Manager Nirjar Poudel and Principal Phoolmaya Budhathoki, who praised the initiative for boosting student confidence and encouraging regular school attendance.
This activity reflects the bank’s continued commitment to education-focused CSR efforts across Nepal. Community participation, including parents and teachers, made the event impactful, especially in a region where economic hardship often limits children’s access to learning tools.
While modest in scale, the initiative had a significant emotional and educational impact, reinforcing the importance of shared responsibility in promoting education. The bank plans to expand such programs in the future, including health camps, digital learning support, and literacy drives, further strengthening the role of private institutions in national development.

Headline: Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Partners with NCHL to Issue NEPALPAY Domestic Cards
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Ltd. has signed an agreement with Nepal Clearing House Limited (NCHL) to become a principal member of the NPS-National Card Switch & Domestic Card Scheme (NEPALPAY Card). The agreement was exchanged between Mr. Bikash Dhungana, COO of Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank, and Mr. Neelesh Man Singh Pradhan, CEO of NCHL.
Following the commercial rollout, the bank will be able to issue and acquire NEPALPAY Cards, which are part of Nepal's domestic card initiative aimed at enhancing interoperability, reducing dependency on international schemes, ensuring data localization, and promoting digital innovation.
NCHL is leading the implementation of this central payment infrastructure and currently serves 54+ BFIs, PSOs, PSPs, and over 100 indirect and technical members. Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank, with its 130 banking outlets and 72 ATMs, is now set to advance its digital service capabilities with this integration.

Headline: Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Introduces Interbank Teller QR for Seamless Withdrawals
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL) has launched an interbank teller QR service to enhance customer convenience. With this new feature, customers can now withdraw cash from Kamana Sewa counters using mobile banking apps of other banks and financial institutions.
The bank has enabled this service through its smart teller QR system, allowing withdrawals from accounts in other banks without needing to visit those banks physically. This innovation simplifies the banking process, saving time and improving ease, safety, and efficiency for customers.

Headline: Insightful Evaluation: Q3 2081/82 Performance Analysis of B-Class Development Banks Unveiled
Full Content:

Karnali Development Bank Limited has not published its report as Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB) has declared it a "problematic institution" and placed its management under direct NRB control. Share trading of Karnali Development Bank has also been suspended.
This analysis aims to meticulously evaluate the financial performance of Nepal's development banks, categorized as "B" class financial institutions, using the unaudited third-quarter reports for the 2081/82 fiscal year.

The third position is secured by Shine Resunga Development Bank (SHINE) with a net profit of Rs. 51.40 Crores. In terms of growth in net profit, Jyoti Bikas Bank (JBBL) achieved the highest growth margin of 101.15% for Q3 of FY 81/82.
At the regional level, Corporate Development Bank (CORBL) reported the highest growth in net profit at 103.90% for Q3 of FY 81/82.
Paid-up capital:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has the highest paid-up capital amounting to Rs. 7.05 Arba among all the development banks, with Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) holding the second-highest paid-up capital at Rs. 5.68 Arba.
On the other hand, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has the lowest paid-up capital of Rs. 26.25 Crores.
Reserve and surplus:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) reported the highest reserve and surplus, totaling Rs. 4.10 Arba. Following MNBBL is Garima Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL) with a reserve of Rs. 3.03 Arba. Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) holds the third position with a reserve of 2.9 Arba.
Meanwhile, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC), Sindhu Bikas Bank (SINDU), and Saptakoshi Development Bank (SAPDBL) have reported negative reserves and surplus.
Deposits from Customers:
Among B-class institutions, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) leads with a total deposit of Rs. 1.13 Kharba, followed by Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) with a deposit of Rs. 85.79 Arba. The overall development banks have collected a total deposit of Rs. 5.95 Kharba.
Loans and Advances to Customers:
As of Q3 2081/82, total loans and advances of development banks reached Rs. 4.77 Kharba, with an average loan of Rs. 31.83 Arba. Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) disbursed the highest loan amount, totaling Rs. 96.03 Arba, followed by Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) with Rs. 69.05 Arba. Shine Resunga Development Limited (SHINE) disbursed Rs. 54.73 Arba, ranking third.
Net interest income:
In terms of Net Interest Income, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) leads with Rs. 3.28 Arba, followed by Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) with Rs. 2.66 Arba, and Shine Resunga Development Bank Limited (SHINE) with Rs. 1.93 Arba. Out of the 15 banks, 8 reported above-industry-average net interest income.

Banks have set aside funds as loan loss provisions and delayed loan repayments for several borrowers.
Total impairment charges amount to Rs. 5.07 Arba for loans and other losses. Among National Level banks, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) shows the highest impairment charge at Rs. 123.38 Crores, with Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) also holding high provisions at Rs. 94.89 Crores.
At the regional level, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) and Sindhu Bikas Bank (SINDU) reported a reversal in impairment charges.
Annualized Earnings per share:
Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) topped the annualized EPS list at Rs. 17.22 per share, followed by Sindhu Bikas Bank Limited (SINDU) with Rs. 18.76 per share.
Net worth per share:
The highest net worth per share is reported by Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) at Rs. 180.24 per share, followed by Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL) with Rs. 163.86 per share and Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL) at Rs. 163.22 per share. The average net worth per share of the 15 banks is Rs. 133.69.
P/E Ratio:
The P/E ratio indicates how much investors are paying for each rupee of the firm’s earnings. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has the lowest P/E ratio at 22.99 times, whereas Corporate Development Bank Limited reports the highest P/E ratio at 422.72 times.
Non-Performing Loans:
Non-performing loans indicate credit risk for banks. Miteri Development Bank Limited (MDB) has the lowest NPL ratio at 0.78%, while Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has the highest at 44.96%.
Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR):
Miteri Development Bank Limited (MDB) reported the highest CAR at 34.19% while Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) reported the negative CAR at 1.14%.
Others:
Cost of Funds, CD Ratio, Base Rates, and Interest Spread:
Cost of Funds:
Corporate Development Bank Limited (CORBL) has the highest Cost of Funds at 7.04%, while Excel Development Bank Limited (EDBL) has the lowest at 4.21%.
CD Ratio:
The Credit-Deposit Ratio shows how much deposit money has been used as loans. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) reports the highest CD ratio of 87.95%, and Corporate Development Bank Limited (CORBL) has the lowest at 69.29%.
Base Rate and Interest Spread:
The base rate, the minimum interest rate banks charge, is highest at Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) with 15.51% and lowest at Excel Development Bank Limited (EDBL) with 6.92%. Meanwhile, Miteri Development Bank Limited (MDB) reports the highest interest spread rate of 4.60%, and Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL) has the lowest at 4.01%.

Headline: KSBBL Unveils 2082 Annual Calendar Featuring Nepal’s Religious Sites and Key Dates
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL) has released its annual calendar for the year 2082, featuring religious sites and temples from various faiths across Nepal.
The calendar, approved by the Nepal Calendar Determination Committee, includes important dates as decided by the committee. A QR code for digital access to the calendar has been shared via the bank's social media and website.

Headline: KSBBL Organizes "Banking & Business" Event to Bridge Gap with Entrepreneurs
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL) successfully conducted the "Banking & Business" program in Kailali to strengthen ties between entrepreneurs and financial institutions. Around 120 business owners participated in the event, which featured discussions with Nepal Rastra Bank officials, KSBBL executives, and industry leaders.
Key topics included:
i. Financial policies and regulations affecting businesses.
ii. Challenges in access to finance for small entrepreneurs.
iii. Nepal Rastra Bank's initiatives for economic stability.
iv. Post-pandemic business recovery strategies.
KSBBL reaffirmed its commitment to enhancing financial accessibility and plans to expand such programs to other regions.

Headline: KSBBL Olympics 2081 Successfully Concludes with Enthusiastic Participation
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Ltd. successfully concluded the KSBBL Olympics 2081, fostering teamwork, sportsmanship, and intellectual growth among employees. The event featured badminton doubles and chess competitions with participants from seven provinces and the central office.
In men's badminton doubles, Surendra Bhandari and Ashish Adhikari from Narayangadh defeated Umesh Ghimire and Sujan Thapaliya from Koshi. In the women's category, Manisha Kumari Shrestha and Anisha Tiwari from Narayangadh triumphed over Ansu Karmacharya and Deepa Chauhan from the central office.
In chess, Prabhakar Pandey from Butwal won the men's title, defeating Sanjeev Lama from Kathmandu, while Nisha Prasai from the central office claimed victory in the women's category, beating Manju Khatri from Koshi.
The winners received trophies, medals, and certificates from Deputy CEO Binay Dahal and COO Bikash Dhungana. Dahal emphasized the role of such events in enhancing employees’ physical and intellectual abilities while strengthening relationships. The bank also organizes an inter-bank futsal cup annually as part of its anniversary celebrations.

Headline: Kamana Sewa Bank Introduces Fixed Deposit Account Opening via Mobile App
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank has launched a convenient feature allowing customers to open fixed deposit accounts through its mobile banking app, KSI Mobile Banking.
This eliminates the need for physical visits, enabling users to open accounts securely from anywhere at any time.
By selecting "Fixed Deposit" and entering the desired amount, customers can complete the process effortlessly.
The bank aims to enhance customer convenience by integrating advanced technology for a faster and more efficient banking experience.

Headline: Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Conducts Breast Cancer Awareness Training for Employees
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited recently organized a breast cancer awareness training for its employees, aimed at promoting early detection and self-assessment. The training, conducted by Dr. Sujita Hirachan, focused on identifying early symptoms of breast cancer, including lumps and unusual changes in the breast, and emphasized the importance of self-examination.
Dr. Hirachan also highlighted that breast cancer can affect both men and women and early detection significantly increases the chances of successful treatment. Employees who have battled cancer shared their personal experiences and encouraged regular screenings every 5-6 months. The bank is committed to continuing such health awareness initiatives to spread cancer awareness and foster a positive outlook within the community.

Headline: Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Conducts Banking & Business Conclave in Collaboration with NYEF Chitwan
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank, in collaboration with NYEF Chitwan, organized the Banking & Business Conclave to bridge the gap between banks and entrepreneurs, with over 60 young entrepreneurs from Chitwan participating.
Speakers, including Deputy CEO Binaya Dahal, FCA Biman Karki, and former NYEF Chitwan President Surya Bhakta Adhikari, discussed financial transparency, regulatory compliance, and post-COVID business challenges. The event highlighted issues like financial literacy, regulatory burdens, and economic constraints.
Calls were made for banks to support struggling businesses, particularly in hospitality, while concerns about infrastructure and youth migration were raised. The conclave concluded with commitments to enhance bank-business collaboration for sustainable growth.

Headline: Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Receives Approval to Issue Unredeemable Non-Cumulative Preference Shares
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank has received approval from Nepal Rastra Bank to issue unredeemable Non-Cumulative Preference Shares. The bank had proposed this in its 18th annual general meeting and submitted it for approval.
The bank will issue 350,000 units of unredeemable Non-Cumulative Preference Shares at a 9% return rate, aiming to increase cash flow and business expansion. These shares will be offered to institutional investors as a viable investment option. After receiving approval from the Securities Board of Nepal, the shares will be listed on the stock exchange.

Headline: Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Partners with Ishan Children & Women’s Hospital for Discounted Services
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank has signed an agreement with Ishan Children & Women’s Hospital Pvt. Ltd., located in Basundhara, Kathmandu, to provide discounted service charges.
Under this agreement, the bank’s employees and customers can avail of a 10% discount on various lab services offered by the hospital. The hospital, established to make healthcare services accessible to the general public, will provide this benefit to the bank’s employees and customers upon presenting proof of their association with the bank. Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank believes that this partnership will offer significant value to all its associated members.

Headline: Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited Enhances Community Support Through CSR Initiative
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited, through its Gargare branch, has donated a computer to the Rudrapur Water Supply Organization as part of its corporate social responsibility.
The handover ceremony, led by Bhim Prasad Tulachan, a board member, saw gratitude expressed by Kanchan Village President Nawaraj Dhakal and Rudrapur Water Supply Organization President Nam Bahadur KC.
Key attendees included Khim Lal Bhusal, the bank's Butwal regional head, and ward presidents of Kanchan Rural Municipality wards 3, 4, and 5. The bank affirmed its commitment to similar initiatives in collaboration with stakeholders in the future.

Headline: Nepal Micro Insurance Company Ltd. Partners with Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank to Expand Financial Services
Full Content:
Nepal Micro Insurance Company Ltd. (NMIC) and Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Ltd. have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to explore collaborative business ventures that benefit both organizations and their customers. The MoU was signed by Mr. Mrigendra Rimal, CEO of NMIC, and Mr. Hari Prasad Lamsal, DGM of Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank, with Mr. Anil Raj Giri, Deputy CEO of NMIC, witnessing the event.
The partnership aims to expand access to insurance and financial solutions, particularly in underserved rural and semi-urban areas, promoting financial inclusion and economic development in Nepal. Both organizations are committed to innovation, customer satisfaction, and high standards of service quality.

Headline: Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Celebrates 18th Anniversary with Nationwide Blood Donation Program and Other Social Initiatives
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank celebrated its 18th anniversary with various programs across the country. A nationwide blood donation drive was held on 27th Kartik, collecting a total of 393 pints of blood from regional and central offices.
The program was inaugurated by Bhim Prasad Tulachan in Butwal, with Binaya Dahal, the bank’s deputy CEO, handing over a blood bag at the central office.
The bank also honored employees who donated the most blood, including Dipendra Subedi, Dandpani Bhattarai, Nitesh Aryal, Rajesh Kuikel, Yagyamurti Luitel, and Yam Bahadur Shrestha.
Other anniversary activities included a week-long monastery cleaning campaign, a dustbin handover, a football cup competition, and financial literacy programs.

Headline: Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Celebrates 18th Anniversary with Financial Literacy Program and Upcoming Blood Donation Drive
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank hosted a financial literacy morning round program on Monday as part of its 18th-anniversary celebrations. The program aimed to educate participants about credit, savings, and banking services.
It took place with employees traveling from the bank's central office in Gyaneshwor, passing through Maitidevi Temple, Dillibazar, and Naxal Bhagwati Temple.
The bank emphasized the importance of helping the community understand financial management and economic opportunities. Additionally, the bank will hold a nationwide blood donation program on Tuesday, 27th, to mark its anniversary.

Headline: Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Successfully Concludes 4th Kamana Sewa Futsal Cup for 18th Anniversary Celebration
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank celebrated its 18th anniversary by hosting the fourth season of the Kamana Sewa Futsal Cup. In the men’s final, Nepal Investment Mega Bank claimed victory over Garima Bikas Bank with a 3-0 score, while in the women’s final, Lumbini Bikas Bank defeated Global IME Bank 2-0.
The bank awarded trophies, medals, and certificates to the winners and runners-up, with 14 men’s teams and 7 women’s teams participating. Bishweshwar Subedi initiated the event by handing the ball to ANFA referee Narayan Adhikari, and Deputy CEO Binay Dahal distributed prizes. To mark its anniversary, the bank will also host a nationwide blood donation program on Tuesday, the 27th.

Headline: Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Partners with Dusit Thani Himalayan Resort Dhulikhel to Offer Exclusive Discounts
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank has partnered with Dusit Thani Himalayan Resort Dhulikhel to offer exclusive 15% discounts to its employees and customers. The discount covers resort amenities such as the restaurant, Devarana Wellness Spa, swimming pool, jacuzzi, steam, and sauna.
To access these benefits, affiliates simply need to present proof of their affiliation with the bank. This collaboration aims to enhance customer satisfaction and provide additional value for the bank’s associates. Headline: Comprehensive Analysis of First Quarter Reports for FY 2081/82: A Closer Look at Development Banks in Nepal
Full Content:
The first-quarter reports for the fiscal year 2081/82 have been publicly disclosed by all 16 development banks. These reports provide a comprehensive overview of their financial health. This analysis aims to meticulously evaluate the financial performance of Nepal's development banks, categorized as "B" class financial institutions, using the unaudited first-quarter reports for the 2081/82 fiscal year.
The Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE) currently lists 16 development banks, divided into National-level and Regional-level entities. Our focus is on assessing the performance of these "B" class financial institutions, drawing insights from the recently released quarter-end reports.
Net profit:
As per the quarterly report, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has reported the highest net profit for the period, amounting to Rs. 28.18 Crores. Shine Resunga Development Bank (SHINE) comes in second place in terms of profit, which amounts to Rs. 23.94 Crores.
The third position is secured by Garima Bikas Bank (GBBL) with a net profit of Rs. 22.57 Crores. In terms of growth in net profit, Jyoti Bikas Bank (JBBL) achieved the highest growth margin of 197.62% for the Q1 of FY 81/82.
At the regional level, Sindhu Bikas Bank (SINDU) reported the highest growth in net profit at 1100.52% for Q1 of FY 81/82.
Paid-up capital:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has the highest paid-up capital amounting to Rs. 7.05 Arba among all the development banks, with Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) holding the second-highest paid-up capital at Rs. 5.68 Arba.
On the other hand, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has the lowest paid-up capital of Rs. 26.25 Crores.
Reserve and surplus:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) reported the highest reserve and surplus, totaling Rs. 3.81 Arba. Following MNBBL is Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) with a reserve of Rs. 3.52 Arba. Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) holds the third position with a reserve of 3.39 Arba.
Meanwhile, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC), Sindhu Bikas Bank (SINDU), and Saptakoshi Development Bank (SAPDBL) have reported negative reserves and surplus.
Deposits from Customers:
Among B-class institutions, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) leads with a total deposit of Rs. 1.10 Kharba, followed by Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) with a deposit of Rs. 83.27 Arba. The overall development banks have collected a total deposit of Rs. 5.9 Kharba.
Loans and Advances to Customers:
As of Q1 2081/82, total loans and advances of development banks reached Rs. 4.74 Kharba, with an average loan of Rs. 29.65 Arba. Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) disbursed the highest loan amount, totaling Rs. 94.72 Arba, followed by Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) with Rs. 68.42 Arba. Shine Resunga Development Limited (SHINE) disbursed Rs. 53.74 Arba, ranking third.
Net interest income:
In terms of Net Interest Income, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) leads with Rs. 1.11 Arba, followed by Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) with Rs. 98.68 Crores, and Shine Resunga Development Bank Limited (SHINE) with Rs. 65.89 Crores. Out of the 16 banks, 8 reported above-industry-average net interest income.
Provisions for the period (Impairment/Reversal):
Banks have set aside funds as loan loss provisions and delayed loan repayments for several borrowers.
Total impairment charges amount to Rs. 1.85 Arba for loans and other losses. Among National Level banks, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) shows the highest impairment charge at Rs. 38.77 Crores, with Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) also holding high provisions at Rs. 37.21 Crores.
At the regional level, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) and Sindhu Bikas Bank (SINDU) reported a reversal in impairment charges.
Annualized Earnings per share:
Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) topped the annualized EPS list at Rs. 22.97 per share, followed by Shine Resunga Development Bank Limited (SHINE) with Rs. 20.23 per share.
Net worth per share:
The highest net worth per share is reported by Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) at Rs. 196.57 per share, followed by Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL) with Rs. 163.48 per share and Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL) at Rs. 154.21 per share. The average net worth per share of the 16 banks is Rs. 129.64.

Non-Performing Loans:
Non-performing loans indicate credit risk for banks. Miteri Development Bank Limited (MDB) has the lowest NPL ratio at 1.80%, while Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has the highest at 34.81%.
Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR):
Corporate Development Bank Limited (CORBL) reported the highest CAR at 34.95%, while Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) reported the lowest at 4.58%.
Others:

Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has the highest Cost of Funds at 7.82%, while Excel Development Bank Limited (EDBL) has the lowest at 4.92%.

The Credit-Deposit Ratio shows how much deposit money has been used as loans. Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) reports the highest CD ratio of 87.72%, and Karnali Development Bank Limited (KRBL) has the lowest at 59.81%.
Base Rate and Interest Spread:

Headline: Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited to Receive South Asian Federation of Accountants Award 2023
Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited has received the "Certificate of Merit Award" from the South Asian Federation of Accountants (SAFA) for its exceptional performance in the financial services sector, based on its fiscal year 2022-23 annual report.
The award will be presented on November 11, 2024, in Colombo, Sri Lanka. SAFA evaluates financial statements from South Asia and awards various categories, involving chartered accountant bodies from eleven countries, including Nepal.
The bank's detailed reporting at its 17th Annual General Meeting contributed to this recognition. Headline: Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited Holds 18th Annual General Meeting
Full Content:

Full Content:

The discount can be accessed at the Buddha Air counter and applied by scanning a QR code via the bank's mobile banking or using the bank's debit and credit cards.
The bank anticipates that this agreement will benefit all associated dignitaries. The agreement was signed by Deputy General Manager Hari Prasad Lamsal and Buddha Air's Marketing Sales Director Rupesh Joshi.

Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank, as part of its corporate social responsibility, has transferred 63 pots to the Prashanti Tole Bikash Sastha through its Damak, Jhapa branch. This initiative aims to promote a clean environment by encouraging the planting of a pot plant in front of every house.

Headline: Financial Showdown: A Comparative Deep Dive into Development Banks' Q4 Performance for FY 2080/81
Full Content:
The fourth-quarter reports for the fiscal year 2080/81 have been publicly disclosed by 16 development banks, with the notable exception of
Karnali Development Bank (KRBL)
, which has yet to release its quarter-end report. These reports provide a comprehensive overview of their financial health. Net profit:
As per the quarterly report, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has reported the highest net profit for the period amounting to Rs. 1.27 Arba. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) comes in second place in terms of profit which amounts to Rs. 1.13 Arba.
The third position is secured by Shine Resunga Development Bank (SHINE) with a net profit of Rs. 69.74 Crores. In terms of growth in Net profit, Shangrila Development Bank (SADBL) has obtained the highest growth margin of 92.47% for the Q4 of FY 80/81.
Coming towards the regional level, Corporate Development Bank (CORBL) has reported the highest growth in net profit of 194.23% for Q4 of FY 80/81.
Paid-up capital:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has the highest paid-up capital amounting to Rs. 7.05 Arba among all the development banks. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has the second-highest paid-up capital amounting to Rs. 5.68 Arba.
On the other hand, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has the lowest paid-up capital of Rs. 26.25 Crores.
Reserve and surplus:
The reserve is the amount that is retained by the company from its profits to promote future growth.
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has reported the highest reserve and surplus which amounts to Rs. 3.50 Arba. MNBBL is followed by Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) with a total reserve of Rs. 3.26 Arba. Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) has secured the third position with a reserve of 3.11 Arba.
Whereas, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC), Sindhu Bikas Bank (SINDU) and Saptakoshi Development Bank (SAPDBL) have reported negative reserves and surplus.
Deposits from Customers:
In B-class institution, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has topped the list with a total deposit of Rs. 1.09 Kharba. This list is followed by Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) with a total deposit of Rs. 84.25 Arba.
The overall development bank has collected a total deposit of Rs. 5.94 Kharba.
Loans and Advances to Customers:
Till Q4 2080/2081, total loans and advances of development banks stood at Rs. 4.61 Kharba. The average loan stood at Rs. 30.78 Arba.
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has disbursed the highest amount of loans which amounts to Rs. 91.90 Arba. Following the list, Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has disbursed a total loan of Rs. 66.01 Arba. Shine Resunga Development Limited (SHINE) has disbursed a loan of Rs. 52.17 Arba which puts it in third place.
Net interest income:
Net Interest Income is the core business revenue which is calculated by subtracting the cost related to the deposits from the income from loans and advances.
In terms of Net interest income, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) tops the list with a total of Rs. 4.18 Arba. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has the second-highest net interest income amounting to Rs. 3.46 Arba. GBBL is followed by Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL) which has reported a net interest income of Rs. 2.36 Arba.
Out of the 16 banks, 8 banks have reported above-industry-average net interest income.
Provisions for the period (Impairment/Reversal):
Banks have set aside a certain amount in loan loss provision and have delayed the loan repayment of several borrowers. A total of Rs 3.83 Arba has been shown in an impairment charge for a loan and other losses.
In the National Level, Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL) has the highest impairment charge for a loan and other losses with Rs. 95.17 Crores. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) also has higher provisions amounting to Rs. 70.92 Crores.
In the regional level, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) and Sindhu Bikas Bank (SINDU) have reported the lowest impairment charges for this period.
Earnings per share:
Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) topped the list in terms of EPS amounting to Rs. 20 per share. Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL) has the second-highest EPS with Rs. 18.38 per share.
Net worth per share:
The highest net worth per share is reported by Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) with Rs. 188.48 per share. This is followed by Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL) with a net worth per share of Rs. 164.48 per share. Similarly, Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL) reported a net worth of Rs. 160.44 per share.
The average net worth per share comes at Rs. 133.10 per share when we factor in the net worth per share of 16 banks.
P/E Ratio:
The P/E ratio tells investors what they are paying for each rupee of earnings of the firm. The lower the ratio, the better the deal.
In terms of the P/E ratio, Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has the lowest P/E ratio of 19.25 times. Meanwhile, Narayani Development Bank Limited reported the highest P/E of 685.79 times.
One should always check the fundamentals of the company and if they find the bad fundamentals then there is a reason for the lower valuation. Also, the PE is calculated as per the quarter-end closing price of the respective companies. In today's date, the price differs in the secondary market.
Non-Performing Loans:
Non-performing loan indicates the risk of credit provided by the bank to its clients. A higher NPL indicates that the bank might be at risk.
In terms of NPL, Miteri Development Bank Limited (MDB) has the lowest ratio with an NPL of 0.97%, and on the other hand, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has reported the highest NPL of 35%.
Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR):
In terms of the Capital Adequacy ratio (CAR), Corporate Development Bank Limited (CORBL) seems to have reported the highest CAR of 38.65%, while Sindhu Bikas Bank (SINDU) has the lowest CAR of 6.58%.
CAR is the ratio of a bank's capital in relation to its risk-weighted assets and current liabilities.
Others:
Cost of Funds, CD Ratio, Base Rates, and Interest Spread:
Cost of Funds:
The term cost of funds refers to how much banks and financial institutions spend in order to acquire money to lend to their customers. The lower the cost of funds, the better because it ultimately reduces the cost of banks. As per reports, Corporate Development Bank Limited (LBBL) has the highest Cost of Funds at 7.71%, whereas Excel Development Bank Limited (EDBL) has the lowest cost of funds at 5.55%.
CD Ratio:
The CD ratio refers to the credit-deposit ratio in banking parlance. It tells how much of the money banks have raised in the form of deposits has been deployed as loans. Similarly, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has reported the highest CD ratio of 85.83%, whereas Miteri Development Bank Limited (MDB) has reported the lowest CD ratio of 60.56%.
Base Rate and Interest Spread:
Base rate is defined as the minimum interest rate set by the NRB below which banks are not permitted to lend to their customers. Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) reports the highest base rate of 15.33%, and Excel Development Bank Limited (EDBL) has the lowest base rate of 8%.
Likewise, the net interest rate spread represents the variance between the interest rate disbursed to depositors and the interest accrued from loans extended to consumers by a bank. Among the majority of development banks, a consistent interest spread rate of 4.58% has been upheld, with the highest reported at 4.59%.

Full Content:
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank won the silver award for the financial services sector at the National Best Annual Report Award 2023, presented by the Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Chartered Accountant Institute. Headline: Insightful Evaluation: Q3 2080/81 Performance Analysis of B-Class Development Banks Unveiled
Full Content:
The third-quarter reports for the fiscal year 2080/81 have been publicly disclosed by 16 development banks, offering a comprehensive insight into their financial standing. This analysis is poised to meticulously evaluate the financial performance of the Development Banks of Nepal, classified as a "B" class financial institution, leveraging the unaudited third-quarter report for the 2080/81 fiscal year.
The Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE) presently enumerates a total of 16 development banks, distinguished by their categorization into National-level and Regional-level entities. Our scrutiny is squarely centered on assessing the performance of B-class financial institutions within this spectrum, with particular emphasis on gleaned insights from the divulged third-quarter reports.
Net profit:
As per the quarterly report, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has reported the highest net profit for the period amounting to Rs. 87.18 Crores. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) comes in second place in terms of profit which amounts to Rs. 68.35 Crores.
The third position is secured by Shine Resunga Development Bank (SHINE) with a net profit of Rs. 51.47 Crores. In terms of growth in Net profit, Shangrila Development Bank (SADBL) has obtained a growth margin of 9.44% for the Q3 of FY 80/81.
Coming towards the regional level, Green Development Bank (GRDBL) has reported the highest growth in net profit of 74.40% while Corporate Development Bank (CORBL) reported the highest decline in net profit of 33.23% in the Q3 of FY 80/81.
Paid-up capital:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has the highest paid-up capital amounting to Rs. 7.05 Arba among all the development banks. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has the second-highest paid-up capital amounting to Rs. 5.68 Arba.
On the other hand, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has the lowest paid-up capital of Rs. 26.25 Crores.
Reserve and surplus:
The reserve is the amount that is retained by the company from its profits to promote future growth.
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has reported the highest reserve and surplus which amounts to Rs. 3.06 Arba. MNBBL is followed by Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) with a total reserve of Rs. 2.76 Arba. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has secured the third position with a reserve of 2.758 Arba.
Whereas, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) and Saptakoshi Development Bank (SAPDBL) have reported negative reserves and surplus.
Deposits from Customers:
In B-class institution, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has topped the list with a total deposit of Rs. 1.10 Kharba. This list is followed by Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) with a total deposit of Rs. 82.83 Arba.
The overall development bank has collected a total deposit of Rs. 5.83 Kharba.
Loans and Advances to Customers:
Till Q3 2080/2081, total loans and advances of development banks stood at Rs. 4.63 Kharba. The average loan stood at Rs. 28.99 Arba.
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has disbursed the highest amount of loans which amounts to Rs. 92.86 Arba. Following the list, Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has disbursed a total loan of Rs. 64.89 Arba. Shine Resunga Development Limited (SHINE) has disbursed a loan of Rs. 51.68 Arba which puts it in third place.
Net interest income:
Net Interest Income is the core business revenue which is calculated by subtracting the cost related to the deposits from the income from loans and advances.
In terms of Net interest income, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) tops the list with a total of Rs. 3.13 Arba. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has the second-highest net interest income amounting to Rs. 2.51 Arba. GBBL is followed by Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL) which has reported a net interest income of Rs. 1.70 Arba.
Out of the 16 banks, 8 banks have reported above-industry-average net interest income.
Provisions for the period (Impairment/Reversal):
Banks have set aside a certain amount in loan loss provision and have delayed the loan repayment of several borrowers. A total of Rs 4.49 Arba has been shown in an impairment charge for a loan and other losses.
In the National Level, Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL) has the highest impairment charge for a loan and other losses with Rs. 83.03 Crores. Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) also has higher provisions amounting to Rs. 72.92 Crores.
In the regional level, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) and Karnali Development Bank (KRBL) have reported the lowest impairment charges for this period.
Earnings per share:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) topped the list in terms of EPS amounting to Rs. 16.50 per share. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL) has the second-highest EPS with Rs. 16.04 per share.
Net worth per share:
The highest net worth per share is reported by Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) with Rs. 178.61 per share. This is followed by Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL) with a net worth per share of Rs. 156.28 per share. Similarly, Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL) reported a net worth of Rs. 155.34 per share.
The average net worth per share comes at Rs. 127.78 per share when we factor in the net worth per share of 16 banks.
P/E Ratio:
The P/E ratio tells investors what they are paying for each rupee of earnings of the firm. The lower the ratio, the better the deal.
In terms of the P/E ratio, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has the lowest P/E ratio of 20.79 times. Meanwhile, Corporate Development Bank Limited reported the highest P/E of 194.83 times from the regional level.
One should always check the fundamentals of the company and if they find the bad fundamentals then there is a reason for the lower valuation. Also, the PE is calculated as per the quarter-end closing price of the respective companies. In today's date, the price differs in the secondary market.
Non-Performing Loans:
Non-performing loan indicates the risk of credit provided by the bank to its clients. A higher NPL indicates that the bank might be at risk.
In terms of NPL, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has the lowest ratio with an NPL of 2.02%, and on the other hand, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has reported the highest NPL of 31.77%.
Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR):
In terms of the Capital Adequacy ratio (CAR), Corporate Development Bank Limited (CORBL) seems to have reported the highest CAR of 41.99%, while Karnali Development Bank (KRBL) has the lowest CAR of 10.18%.
CAR is the ratio of a bank's capital in relation to its risk-weighted assets and current liabilities.
Others:
Cost of Funds, CD Ratio, Base Rates, and Interest Spread:
Cost of Funds:
The term cost of funds refers to how much banks and financial institutions spend in order to acquire money to lend to their customers. The lower the cost of funds, the better because it ultimately reduces the cost of banks. As per reports, Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) has the highest Cost of Funds at 8.53%, whereas Excel Development Bank Limited (EDBL) has the lowest cost of funds at 6.35%.
CD Ratio:
The CD ratio refers to the credit-deposit ratio in banking parlance. It tells how much of the money banks have raised in the form of deposits has been deployed as loans. Similarly, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has reported the highest CD ratio of 85.89%, whereas Miteri Development Bank Limited (MDB) has reported the lowest CD ratio of 63.49%.
Base Rate and Interest Spread:
Base rate is defined as the minimum interest rate set by the NRB below which banks are not permitted to lend to their customers. Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) reports the highest base rate of 15.09%, and Shine Resunga Development Bank Limited (SHINE) has the lowest base rate of 9.04%.
Likewise, the net interest rate spread represents the variance between the interest rate disbursed to depositors and the interest accrued from loans extended to consumers by a bank. Among the majority of development banks, a consistent interest spread rate of 4.57% has been upheld, with the highest reported at 4.60%.
